title: Local homotopy lifting through a ringed-site cohomology approximation
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a site with a sheaf of commutative rings, with module sheaves and their cochain complexes and cohomology [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $U$ be a site object and restrict to $(\mathcal C/U,\mathcal O_U)$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Let $a\in\mathbf Z$, and let $E^\bullet,F^\bullet,G^\bullet$ be complexes of $\mathcal O_U$-modules with chain maps $u:E^\bullet\to F^\bullet$ and $v:G^\bullet\to F^\bullet$. Assume $E^\bullet$ is zero outside finitely many degrees, every $E^j$ is a direct summand of a finite free $\mathcal O_U$-module, and $E^j=0$ for $j<a$. Suppose $H^j(v)$ is an isomorphism for $j>a$ and is surjective for $j=a$. There is a covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ and chain maps $t_i:E^\bullet|_{U_i}\to G^\bullet|_{U_i}$ such that $v|_{U_i}\circ t_i$ is chain homotopic to $u|_{U_i}$. Explicitly there are maps $s_i^j:E^j|_{U_i}\to F^{j-1}|_{U_i}$ with $u^j|_{U_i}-v^j|_{U_i}t_i^j=d_F^{j-1}s_i^j+s_i^{j+1}d_E^j$ for every $j$. There is no boundedness assumption on $F^\bullet$ or $G^\bullet$.

proof.text: Form $C=C(v)$ with $C^j=F^j\oplus G^{j+1}$ and $d_C(f,g)=(d_F f+v g,-d_G g)$, and let $i:F\to C$ be inclusion. Its cone triangle in $D(\mathcal O_U)$ is distinguished by the definition of the derived triangulated structure. The cited long exact sequence gives $H^j(G)\xrightarrow{H^j(v)}H^j(F)\to H^j(C)\to H^{j+1}(G)\xrightarrow{H^{j+1}(v)}H^{j+1}(F)$. For $j\geq a$ the first arrow is surjective and the last is injective. Exactness makes the map into $H^j(C)$ zero, the next map injective, and its image zero. Thus $H^j(C)=0$ for every $j\geq a$. This argument uses no bounds on $F$ or $G$.

Apply the local null-homotopy lemma to $w=i\circ u:E\to C$ on $(\mathcal C/U,\mathcal O_U)$, with the same $a$. All its source hypotheses are exactly the finite-support, finite-free-retract and lower-bound hypotheses on $E$; Step 1 supplies its target cohomology vanishing. Obtain a covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ and homotopies $h_i^j:E^j|_{U_i}\to C^{j-1}|_{U_i}$ satisfying $(i u)^j=d_C^{j-1}h_i^j+h_i^{j+1}d_E^j$. A covering of the terminal object $U/U$ of the slice is a covering of $U$ in the original site.

On each covering member decompose $h_i^j=(s_i^j,t_i^j)$ using $C^{j-1}=F^{j-1}\oplus G^j$. Restriction is sectionwise, so the cone formula and its two projections restrict to the same formulas on the slice. The $G^j$-component of the homotopy equation is $0=-d_G^j t_i^j+t_i^{j+1}d_E^j$, so the $t_i^j$ form a chain map $t_i:E|_{U_i}\to G|_{U_i}$. The $F^j$-component is $u^j=d_F^{j-1}s_i^j+v^j t_i^j+s_i^{j+1}d_E^j$. Rearranging gives precisely $u^j-v^j t_i^j=d_F^{j-1}s_i^j+s_i^{j+1}d_E^j$. These identities hold in every degree, including the zero source terms, and give the required homotopy.
